Markus — drafting the technical pieces. Quick notes I’ll include in the threat_model_summary.pdf and isolation matrix: 

- Network topology: hosted mode runs in Redwood-managed VPCs per region, with tenant traffic logically separated by mTLS, per-tenant routing tables, and dedicated prefixes. Private (VPC) deployments can be deployed inside customer-managed VPCs; we use PrivateLink or VPC peering depending on routing requirements.

- Data control plane separation: control plane services (account mgmt, billing, orchestration) run in a locked-down management VPC; customer inference dataplane lives in separate GPU-backed subnet groups. The only control-plane -> dataplane call flows are authenticated, short-lived RPCs over internal networks using mutual TLS.

- KV cache & state: ephemeral KV caches are stored in encrypted memory-backed caches on the inference hosts; persistent metadata stored in customer-scoped databases encrypted at rest. Cross-region replication is async and uses encrypted transport with per-region CMKs.

- Key management: KMS integration available — hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys or bring-your-own KMS (BYOK) via customer key rings and HSM-backed providers. Private deployments can integrate with customer HSMs.

- Threat model highlights (short):
  * Attacker goals: token exfiltration, model theft, data leakage across tenants.
  * Primary mitigations: strict isolation (network + process), KV/cache eviction policies, per-request authentication and authorization, streaming token scrubbing for logs, and E2E encryption.
  * Residual risks: misconfiguration of customer-managed networking, and side-channel risks on shared hardware (mitigated via dedicated pools/tenant pinning).

Attachments: initial diagram PNG (annotated draft) and short threat model draft (PDF). I’ll add the isolation matrix XLSX next.

—
Dylan Brooks
Security Architect — Redwood Inference

Luke — attaching the deliverables per our plan. Files attached to this message and also uploaded to a shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cZenith-Redwood-Shared

Included artifacts (attached):
- zenith_network_diagram_v2.png (annotated) — shows both a Hosted-mode example and a Private-mode deployment pinned into a customer VPC. Callouts include: NAT egress points, centralized logging collectors (ingress-only), and cross-region replication lanes labeled.
- isolation_model_matrix.xlsx — rows include: tenant identifier surface, network controls, compute isolation, data-at-rest encryption, key management, admin controls, audit log retention. Columns show Hosted / Dedicated / Private profiles.
- threat_model_summary.pdf — two pages summarizing attacker goals, mitigations, and residual risks. It calls out side-channel protections (dedicated pools option), KMS options (BYOK/HSM), and recommended guardrails for customers (least privilege IAM, subnets/ACLs).

Key clarifications you asked about cross-region replication and KMS:
- Cross-region replication is asynchronous; data-in-transit is encrypted with TLS1.3 and application-layer signing. Each region uses distinct CMKs; we support rotatable keys. For Hosted customers who prefer not to share keys, BYOK is available via KMIP/HSM integrations.
- For Private deployments inside a customer VPC, control plane connectivity is restricted to pub-sub over PrivateLink or peered interfaces; telemetry can be routed to customer logging accounts.

If you want a single-page executive diagram instead of the full PNG, tell me and we’ll produce a condensed one.

Attachments: [zenith_network_diagram_v2.png] [isolation_model_matrix.xlsx] [threat_model_summary.pdf]

Markus / team — thank you, this is exactly what we needed and the level of detail is helpful. A couple of quick follow-ups before we close the RFP packet:

1) On the isolation_matrix, can you add a short note (one line) explaining how Redwood prevents lateral movement between tenant workloads in the Hosted shared pools? You mentioned tenant pinning; a sentence describing enforcement (e.g., network ACL + cgroup/process limits + hypervisor isolation when applicable) would be great.

2) For Private deployments, can you confirm whether Redwood requires any inbound ports from our management plane, or whether management calls are all outbound from our VPC (preferred)?

If you can reply with those clarifications in the next 24 hours, we’ll finalize and upload to our procurement portal.

Best,
Luke
